overall_reason: The hero runs a word-by-word heading reveal, a 5.5 s shimmer on the accent words, three floating colour orbs (18 to 26 s), an 11 s sheen sweep, four rising sparks and a pinging "Live" dot all at once, and cards add a lift plus a sheen on hover; the product-preview tab (180 ms ease-out, 12 px) is the one motion with a clear job.

score.reason: T-LOOPS and T-MOTION-BUDGET find six decorative loops in the first screen, T-HOVER-SIGNAL finds shine and lift on cards, and T-MOTION-SYSTEM finds Tailwind defaults on 165 elements.

findings.title: Loops show a state or real data
findings.evidence: Running animations at 1440 include hero-motion-float-a, -b and -c (18 s, 22 s and 26 s, on orbs 578, 466 and 332 px wide), hero-motion-sheen-sweep (11 s infinite, a band 934 x 1685 px), and hero-motion-spark-rise on four 6 px dots (9 to 13.5 s infinite). The stylesheet counts 30 infinite animations.
findings.before: Orbs, a sheen band and sparks loop forever behind the hero.
findings.after: Cut the orbs, the sheen and the sparks; keep a still background.
findings.why: None of these loops shows a state or data, and they compete with the headline and the product preview on every visit.

findings.title: Motion has a budget per page
findings.evidence: In one screen the page runs a load reveal (hero-word-in 620 ms on 8 words plus hero-rise 620 ms on 3 blocks), a shimmer loop on the accent words (hero-word-shimmer 5.5 s infinite, starting at 1.4 s), 3 floating orbs, a sheen sweep, 4 sparks and a "ping" on the "Live" dot (1 s infinite). That is at least six primitives and more than two self-moving things at once.
findings.before: Six or more motion primitives in the first screen.
findings.after: Keep one load moment (the heading reveal or the preview arriving) and the "Live" ping, and cut the rest.
findings.why: When everything moves, nothing is marked as important, and the product preview loses the visitor's attention.

findings.title: The page arrives once and is never gated
findings.where: hero h1 "Everything your team runs on, in one workspace", 1440
findings.evidence: Each word of the h1 animates hero-word-in (opacity 0 to 1, translateY 0.5em, 620 ms on cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 1)), and the accent words then start a 5.5 s gradient shimmer that never stops.
findings.before: The headline rises word by word and then shimmers forever.
findings.after: Show the headline at once; if one entrance stays, fade the whole block once and drop the shimmer.
findings.why: A word-by-word heading rise and a gradient shimmer are the stock generated hero, and the shimmer keeps moving under the text while people read it.

findings.title: Hover answers with one small signal
findings.evidence: The stylesheet declares ".landing-card:hover { transform: translateY(-6px) }" with a larger coloured shadow, and ".landing-card:hover::before" runs landing-sheen (0.9 s, a light band sliding across the card). Hovering the hero stage also brightens the orbs and sparks.
findings.before: Cards lift 6 px, glow and run a sheen on hover.
findings.after: Use one signal, such as a border colour change at about 150 ms; drop the lift, glow and sheen.
findings.why: Lift plus glow plus shine on every card is the decorative hover kit and says nothing about which card the visitor is about to open.

findings.title: One curve family and one duration scale
findings.evidence: 165 of 173 transitioning elements use Tailwind's default cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) at 150 or 200 ms, 7 use the browser default ease (400 and 600 ms), and the hero and cards add cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 1) and cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1). The cookie dialog opens on ease (sweep MOT-002 easing hit).
findings.before: Framework defaults next to two hand-picked curves, with no shared tokens.
findings.after: Choose one exit curve and one duration scale and apply it to the buttons, the cookie dialog and the cards.
findings.why: Unrelated curves for the same kind of change make the controls feel inconsistent next to a hand-tuned hero.

strengths: The product-preview tabs ("Tasks") swap their panel in 180 ms on ease-out with 12 px travel, a short feedback motion that fits a control visitors click several times.
The stylesheet has 11 prefers-reduced-motion rules that switch off the bounce and hero letter animations.
